metric.core_tooling_availability_quality.candidate_universe: Preserved candidate universe and findings from certified legacy work unit ecosystem-tooling--part-1--python; recertification did not select a new language-specific target.

component_findings.build_execute: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--python): Measures maturity, availability, and quality of the core first-party/de-facto-standard developer tooling stack that is NOT already covered by the separate Debugger/Profiler Support metric or the separate Package/Dependency Management metric: (1) official interpreter/runtime implementation, (2) standardized build/compile tooling, (3) linter tooling, (4) formatter tooling, (5) test framework, (6) static type-checking tooling. Excludes debugger/profiler products (scored under metric.debugger_profiler_support) and excludes the package manager / registry (scored under metric.package_dependency_management_quality) to avoid double counting per the Ecosystem spec's mixed-concept split.
component_findings.diagnostic_quality: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--python): By 2026 the toolchain has consolidated around fast Rust-based tools (uv, Ruff) for performance-critical parts alongside mature Python libraries (pytest, mypy) for the rest.
component_findings.docs_package: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--python): Measures maturity, availability, and quality of the core first-party/de-facto-standard developer tooling stack that is NOT already covered by the separate Debugger/Profiler Support metric or the separate Package/Dependency Management metric: (1) official interpreter/runtime implementation, (2) standardized build/compile tooling, (3) linter tooling, (4) formatter tooling, (5) test framework, (6) static type-checking tooling. Excludes debugger/profiler products (scored under metric.debugger_profiler_support) and excludes the package manager / registry (scored under metric.package_dependency_management_quality) to avoid double counting per the Ecosystem spec's mixed-concept split.
component_findings.format_lint: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--python): Ruff has become the recommended unified linter+formatter for new Python projects, replacing the Flake8/Black/isort/pyupgrade patchwork.
component_findings.test: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--python): Test framework: existence of a mature, actively maintained, de-facto-standard test framework plus a built-in/standard-library fallback.

metric.core_tooling_availability_quality.limitations: Scores reflect a single analyst's reading of the frozen sub-criteria against 2026 secondary-source writeups plus one primary source (python.org/Wikipedia CPython) rather than a full independent hands-on tooling audit; multiple competing tools (mypy vs pyright vs ty) were credited as ecosystem strength but also reflect some fragmentation, reflected in the lower static-type-checking sub-score.
metric.core_tooling_availability_quality.selection_rule: Evaluate the maintained first-party/de-facto core developer toolchain actually available today; score implemented capability, not planned design.

metric.package_dependency_management_qua.candidate_universe: Preserved candidate universe and findings from certified legacy work unit ecosystem-tooling--part-1--python; recertification did not select a new language-specific target.

component_findings.manifest_constraints: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--python): An independent 2026 statistical analysis found PyPI contains 736,344 packages with at least one version, up from 311,063 in 2021.
component_findings.publish_version: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--python): Poetry manages dependency installation, virtual environments, package building and publishing, reading configuration from pyproject.toml.
component_findings.registry_security: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--python): Measures the maturity, activity, and quality of the package registry and dependency-management tooling: registry scale/availability, package-manager tool maturity and standardization, dependency resolution/reproducibility (lockfile support), and supply-chain security posture. Package-manager-agnostic dependency *semantics* (e.g. version-range syntax simplicity) are scored under Language Quality, not here; this metric scores the surrounding tool/registry maturity.
component_findings.resolver_lock: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--python): uv only re-runs dependency installation when pyproject.toml or the uv.lock lockfile changes, giving reproducible, cached installs.
component_findings.workspace_multi: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-1--python): Poetry manages dependency installation, virtual environments, package building and publishing, reading configuration from pyproject.toml.

metric.package_dependency_management_qua.limitations: Registry package-count figures vary across sources within 2026 (roughly 736k-899k depending on snapshot date and counting method); the range rather than a single cherry-picked figure is used as declared evidence, consistent with the requirement not to rely on a single raw popularity number as the sole proxy. Tooling fragmentation across pip/Poetry/uv/conda (multiple coexisting package managers) is reflected as a moderate deduction in the resolution/reproducibility and package-manager-maturity sub-scores rather than being ignored.
metric.package_dependency_management_qua.selection_rule: Evaluate the standard/de-facto package workflow using official documentation and current registry/tool behavior; ecosystem size is scored elsewhere.

snapshot_recertification.policy: legacy evidence re-adjudicated under current runner-owned rubric
